chunks: Ibn al-Walid, from al-Saffar and Sa'd together, from Ibn Isa, from his father, and al-Husayn b. Sa'id and Muhammad al-Barqi, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham b. Salim who said:

I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). He said to me: Can you describe Allah? I said: Yes. He said: Bring it forth. I said: He is The Hearing, The Seeing. He said: This is an attribute shared by the created beings. I said: So how do we describe Him? He said: He is Light with no darkness in Him, Life with no death in Him, Knowledge with no ignorance in Him, Truth with no falsehood in Him. I came out from him being the most knowledgeable of people in Tawhid.
ai.seo_question: How does the Imam describe Allah's essence to distinguish it from creation?
ai.summary: This hadith illustrates the Shia theological principle of *tanzih* (divine transcendence) by distinguishing between attributes shared with creation (*sifat al-dhat*) and those unique to Allah. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) critiques the sufficiency of sensory attributes like hearing and seeing, which imply limitation, and instead offers a metaphysical description of God as pure Light, Life, Knowledge, and Truth, free from their opposites. This narrative reinforces the concept of *tawhid al-sifat*, emphasizing that divine attributes are not merely additions to His essence but are identical to it in their perfection.
